mechanism_narrative: A high employment level (PAYEMS) relative to historical averages indicates robust labor market conditions supporting consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS exceeds the 10-year average, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.5% signals monetary tightening, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) above 12-month averages indicate accelerating consumer demand, boosting corporate revenue growth and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS exceed 12-month averages, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Manufacturing contraction indicated by INDPRO below 100 reflects reduced output capacity, lowering corporate earnings and causing negative S&P 500 returns during supply contraction regimes.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: High consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) relative to historical averages indicates eroding purchasing power and potential central bank intervention, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds the 10-year average, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 4.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate revenue, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 4.5%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent housing starts (HOUST) above 1300 and GDP (GDPC1) above 23500 billion dollars indicates expanding economic activity, boosting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when both HOUST > 1300 and GDPC1 > 23500, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS exceeding 0.2 percentage points over 3 months defines a monetary tightening cycle, raising borrowing costs and reducing equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.2pp in 3 months, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
